subject: scope of mcmc::chains methods for statistics

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: scope of mcmc::chains methods for statistics
parts:
We're going to have full getters for warmup,
post-warmup, per-chain, etc. So you'll be able
to do all the stats in R that you'd like.

What kind of methods need to be supported?

Here's the current plan for getters:

---------------------------------
// consistent permutations across calls if no
// samples were added in betweent;
void get_samples_permuted(size_t n, // param
vector<double>& samples);

// post-warmup in original order by chain
void get_samples(size_t n,
size_t k, // chain
vector<double>& samples);

// warmup in original order
void get_warmup_samples(size_t n,
size_t k,
vector<double>& samples);

// get as structure; need to know variable type to pass in
template <typename T>
void get_struct_samples_permuted(size_t j,
vector<T>& samples);

// for chain k, no permutation
template <typename T>
void get_struct_samples(size_t j,
size_t k,
vector<T>& samples);
------------------------------------------------

I should have all this done in the next couple of hours.

I'm tempted to make this it for the mcmc::chains() object
so that it's just a container. Everything else would
then be done on the outside through the returned vectors.
It won't be as efficient, but it seems like much less
duplicated effort.

Here's the list of stats I know we need to calculate:

------------------------------------------
double mean(size_t n);

double sd(size_t n);

void quantiles(size_t n,
const vector<double>& probs,
vector<double>& quantiles);
double quantile(size_t n,
double prob);

pair<double,double> central_interval(size_t n,
double prob);

pair<double,double> smallest_interval(size_t n,
double prob);

double potential_scale_reduction(size_t n)

double split_potential_scale_reduction(size_t n);

double effective_sample_size(size_t n);

double mcmc_error_mean(size_t n);

double autocorrelation(size_t n,
size_t k);
--------------------------------------------------

Anything else anyone thinks we might need?

And if we're going to do all the graphs in R2WinBUGS, we
either need to do a lot more in R, or add an argument
of type size_t for the chain ID.

- Bob

I was thinking that Jiqiang could implement these graphs using ggplot2. If you want we could have some basic graphical summary in the c++; I don't know how hard that would be.

Also traceplots but that's something different. In R, here's what I'm imagining:

print(foo): spits out a table of all the parameters with posterior mean, sd, quantiles, median, spin, R.hat, n.eff. Vector or array parameters are listed one element at a time, e.g., alpha[1,1], then alpha[1,2], etc.

plot(foo): spits out a grid of graphs, basically a prettier version of the right-hand side of the current R2Winbugs output, using some color scheme to indicate R.hat.

traceplot(foo,list_of_parameters): spits out traceplots for specified parameters. We also might want the ability to do 2-d traceplots. In any case, traceplots are great but I don't want them to be the default for plot() as they can be overwhelming for a big model.

Here's some code that uses ggplot2 for caterpillar plots; perhaps you
can use it.

# tab is a data.frame with columns:
# f1, the factor indicating each caterpillar
# avg, the mean or median for the dot in the middle of each caterpillar
# lb, the left tail of the caterpillar (e.g., the lower bound of the 95% CI)
# ub, the right tail

gg <- ggplot(tab, aes(x=f1, y=avg)) +
geom_pointrange(aes(ymin=lb, ymax=ub), pch=1) +
coord_flip()
gg

I do love the "the Caterpillar Plot Should Be Mothballed"
part of the title.

I'm not so convinced by the funnel plot, though. Ordering
the points on the x axis by confidence interval isn't
exactly how we're thinking about posterior intervals in our
model.

All the data and accessors and statistics will be
available programatically as with Coda, so you should
be able to plot however you want.

- Bob
